- Lower abdominal tenderness, most pronounced in lower quadrants  
- Cervical motion tenderness present  
- Purulent cervical discharge observed  
- Leukocyte count elevated at 15,000/mm³  
- ESR markedly elevated at 100 mm/h

- Urine or serum β-hCG result — critical to exclude pregnancy (especially ectopic) before initiating doxycycline and to guide management  
- Pelvic ultrasound findings — pending; needed to assess for tubo-ovarian abscess, hydrosalpinx, or alternative pathology (e.g., ovarian torsion, appendiceal abscess)  
- Adnexal tenderness assessment — not performed; would further support PID but is not required for diagnosis per CDC  
- CRP value — not reported; would add corroborative evidence of inflammation but is redundant given elevated WBC and ESR  
- Results of NAAT for *C. trachomatis* and *N. gonorrhoeae* — pending; confirmation would strengthen etiologic diagnosis but is not required for clinical diagnosis or treatment initiation  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

This 17-year-old AFAB adolescent presents with a classic triad for PID per CDC diagnostic criteria: lower abdominal tenderness, cervical motion tenderness, and purulent cervical discharge — all explicitly documented.
